chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from some of our companions, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Sama'a, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

key_terms.بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِنَا: Some of our companions — an anonymizing formula used in al-Kafi when a transmitter is unnamed but trusted
key_terms.مِثْلَهُ: Similar to it — a technical reference indicating this hadith carries the same content as the preceding one, used to confirm a ruling through multiple chains

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on hunting prey that falls into water or off a mountain after being shot?
ai.summary: This hadith is a supporting transmission providing an alternative chain of narrators (isnad) for a ruling on hunting already stated in a preceding hadith in the same chapter. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) is the ultimate authority. The phrase 'similar to it' (مِثْلَهُ) indicates the legal ruling is identical to what was transmitted before — concerning a hunter who shoots prey that then falls into water or tumbles from a mountain. Al-Kulayni recorded multiple chains to strengthen the authenticity of the ruling.
